body:
T43 H process-evidence clarification under D-WORKFLOW-233 — continue the authorized lane scope

Yes: completed own-lane source-producer evidence plus fresh confined inode/content checks suffices for the exact authorized T43 roots, subject to the conditions below. The stream required the lane's own process/owner records; an all-same-UID cwd/fd census was an added implementation requirement. Its PermissionError is neither proof of a live T43 reference nor proof of no reference. Do not claim every same-UID process was inspected or that PID2389 is unrelated.

Root read the actual candidate and original control/plan failures, and the immutable D application-run, application-overlay-run and partial-control-v2-run receipts: all three have finished timestamps and exit0. Original retirement.py SHA2562b98e817e600b31cbe213cb03e063fc51697ee56eadbcfb8ddb91ede682991a8 and control-run rc1/stderr304a35c54e67eae80ca8ac34f72914a399bf610ff373b2b2be590c50c2b10483 are retained as observations, not a passed cleanup guard. No production deletion or fresh host/process inspection was performed by root.

1. Retain those original program bytes, failure receipts and tiny F scratch creation. Confirm the failed guard/control invocation is finished before editing it. Add a separately identifiable own-lane process scope; do not silently turn PermissionError into an empty successful global scan.

2. Bind every proposed root to its existing custody evidence and completed producing command. Record all current known T43 jobs/descendants that could touch it and their actual termination/no-reference evidence, including new F controls. Use recorded PID/start identities where they exist; do not invent missing historical IDs. A completion receipt proves the named invocation returned, not arbitrary untracked daemons. If a relevant command could have left an unaccounted child or a root has been handed to another consumer, retain that root until accounted for. No other lane has been assigned these source projections by this coordinator.

3. A known relevant T43 owner that is live, has a cwd/fd reference, cannot be inspected where that inspection is needed, or has ambiguous identity blocks the affected root. A genuinely unowned/unassigned same-UID process is outside the required census; do not inspect it further, elevate privileges or infer its references. Record the original inaccessible-process limitation separately and state that no all-same-UID no-reference assertion is available. Do not exempt a known T43 process merely because access fails.

4. Keep all existing path/custody/cache/receipt/symlink/mount/owner/content/identity guards. Retain a new tiny actual-own-FD refusal, missing/ambiguous own-completion refusal, inaccessible known-owner refusal and positive own-lane case after the FD is closed. Demonstrate that an out-of-scope access failure cannot manufacture a global-clean claim. These new record/cleanup controls may run; no accepted A–D producer or test replay. Bind exact new code, inputs, outputs and exits.

5. Rebuild and commit the exact cleanup plan before mutation, with the process evidence scope and limitation explicit. Recheck identity/content immediately before each deletion. Any root failing a required predicate stays retained with its exact reason; retained-root outcomes do not become retired. The four empty prefixes still have only the narrow fresh-current-state/nonrecursive-rmdir authority. Preserve caches and durable receipts, including both publication packets. The failed F scratch is eligible only after its own creation/final-content/termination evidence is complete; do not overwrite its earlier receipt with a new attempt.

Continue F/G/H under this clarification. This changes no source, PL001 outcome,93 input-gap qualification or final acceptance criterion; it defines the evidence scope of the already authorized cleanup. Keep all unresolved roots/limits visible in the final handback. Root final acceptance and any later cleanup beyond these predicates remain separate. No host-ledger/runtime/physical/cloud/provider action or permission response.
